method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 31 covers 12th-15th, sheet 37 covers 15th-18th; 15th is the only shared street, and both plates print '15TH ST.' in it (sheet 31 bottom edge, sheet 37 top edge). Address runs pin the block and the avenue: sheet 31's north frontage of 15th reads 1314 1316 1318 1320 1322 1324 then, across Avenue M (printed 70'), 1402 1404 1406 1408 1410 1412 | 1414 1416 1418 1420 1422; sheet 37's south frontage of the same corridor reads 1311 1313 1315 1317 1319 1321 1323 then 1401 1403 1405 1407 1409 1411 | 1413 1415 1417 1419 1421, with the Avenue M corner numbers 1501 1502 1503 1504 turning the corner. Even numbers north, odd numbers south, and the 1300/1400 hundred-block break falls on Avenue M on both sheets - so the two frontages face each other across one and the same street. One street north on sheet 31 is 14th (faces 2398/2643) and one south on sheet 37 is 16th (faces 1237/1482); neither is shared. Detection's candidates (31: 3233/2104/976; 37: 660/1731/2803) miss the corridor and were discarded. Positions are the mid-line of the 80' corridor from its two block-face rules: sheet 31 y=3555 and y=3796 -> 3676; sheet 37 y=89 and y=332 -> 211.
